chapter.title: From the Dead
chapter.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 to the PowerPyx 100% chart (19 nodes) and the game’s text (the detroitbecometext template: 2 prompts, 13 readouts, no arrow). BACK TO LIFE → ANALYZE SELF → REPAIR LEGS → HEAR ABOUT JERICHO → PASSAGE OF LIMBS → JUNKYARD → [ SEARCH FOR PARTS ] → CLIMB SLOPE → MARKUS CAME BACK FROM THE DEAD, the only ending. Inside the search, in any order: FIND OPTICAL UNIT → CRANE DUMPS BODIES → DIG YOURSELF OUT; FIND AUDIO PROCESSOR; ANDROID BEGS TO DIE (REFUSE TO KILL or KILL, a man); FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID (REFUSE TO KILL FOR PUMP or KILL FOR PUMP, a woman); FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN DEAD ANDROID after sparing her. No probability, timer, failure, relationship, public-opinion or instability change. Cross-chapter: the key to find Jericho (Jericho), the blue eye and the removed LED. Researched in docs/research/chapters/ch11-from-the-dead.md.

decisions.title: Back to Life (checkpoint) and Analyze Self
decisions.context: Markus reboots in the landfill at 03:34 AM, 6 November 2038, after the police shot him in Broken, and diagnoses himself: OPTICAL UNIT impaired (CORRUPTED MIND PALACE), AUDIO PROCESSOR DAMAGED, THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR DEFECTIVE (all systems in LOW POWER MODE), LEFT AND RIGHT LEG COMPONENTS MISSING.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: The start node and checkpoint, then the four diagnosis spots, all required, any order.

decisions.gate: Chapter start, after Fugitives; plays the same after either Broken ending.
decisions.note: Chart nodes BACK TO LIFE (checkpoint) and ANALYZE SELF (action).

benchmark.note: Two narrated events; the template’s four Diagnose readouts are quoted. No stat change.

decisions.title: Repair Legs
decisions.context: Markus examines the legs in the pit: RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6847j FUNCTIONAL COMPATIBLE, #6321t DAMAGED INCOMPATIBLE, LEFT LEG COMPONENT #8427g FUNCTIONAL COMPATIBLE, and fits the two compatible ones.

options.label: REPAIR LEGS
options.effect: Button prompts; nothing can go wrong (PowerPyx).

benchmark.note: A narrated event with the three readouts. No risk.

decisions.title: Hear About Jericho
decisions.context: A dying android (the wiki’s Phileas) grabs Markus: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find Jericho! Find Jericho!..” and passes him a copy of his key to find Jericho before shutting down for good.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Markus carries the key to Jericho from now on.

decisions.note: Chart event HEAR ABOUT JERICHO. Jericho (chapter 14) replays it as a flashback.

decisions.title: Passage of Limbs
decisions.context: Markus squeezes through a tight chasm of android bodies while dying androids’ hands try to hold him down: “Where are you going?”

options.label: PASSAGE OF LIMBS
options.effect: Button prompts; no failure branch on the chart.

decisions.title: Junkyard (checkpoint)
decisions.context: The open junkyard: broken androids repeating their service phrases (one: “I have to get to Jericho...”), the crane, the VETA sign, and the slippery slope that is the way out once the optical unit, audio processor and pump regulator are replaced.

benchmark.note: A narrated event quoting the template’s background lines.

decisions.title: Search for Parts
decisions.context: The bracketed phase: the three parts in any order, the two encounters in the middle, optional looks at incompatible parts (#9754h, #9474, #4807), then the slope.

options.label: FIND OPTICAL UNIT
options.effect: Crane dumps bodies, dig yourself out, blue-iris eye #8087q.

options.label: Middle of the junkyard
options.effect: Android begs to die, then the pump regulator in the android.

options.label: CLIMB SLOPE
options.effect: Needs all three parts; ends the search.

decisions.note: Chart bracket [ SEARCH FOR PARTS ]; the chart draws no order between its branches.

benchmark.note: A repeatable scene (clue state fromDeadSearch). The middle cuts in with the two choices and returns. Each visit says which parts still need replacing.

decisions.title: Android Begs to Die
decisions.context: A crawling android (male) grabs Markus’s leg: “I’m begging you, please… End it… I don’t wanna live anymore…”

options.label: KILL
options.effect: KILL: “Make it quick…”; Markus pulls out his thirium pump and he shuts down. Chart node KILL. No stat change.

options.label: SPARE
options.effect: SPARE: “No, please… Don’t leave me!.. Don’t leave me!”; he is left alive. Chart node REFUSE TO KILL. No stat change.

decisions.gate: In the game optional and easy to miss; the wiki says before replacing parts, PowerPyx meets him after the optical unit.
decisions.note: Chart event ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and choice group REFUSE TO KILL / KILL; the template’s prompt KILL / SPARE. The wiki’s Sorrowful Android.

benchmark.note: Always met on the way to the middle of the junkyard, before the pump android. Records fromDeadBeggar.

decisions.title: Find Pump Regulator in Android
decisions.context: An android (female) with a compatible regulator (#2886) wakes as Markus reaches for it: “Wait! Please! Please, don’t do that! I wanna live…”

options.label: KILL
options.effect: KILL: Markus takes the regulator and she shuts down; his pump is replaced. Chart node KILL FOR PUMP. No stat change.

options.label: SPARE
options.effect: SPARE: “Thank you…”; he must find another regulator. Chart node REFUSE TO KILL FOR PUMP. No stat change.

decisions.gate: In the middle of the junkyard, a few steps from the android who begs to die.
decisions.note: Chart node FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID and choice group REFUSE TO KILL FOR PUMP / KILL FOR PUMP; the template’s prompt KILL / SPARE. The wiki’s Begging Android. No timer in any source.

benchmark.note: Optional: met only by going to the middle of the junkyard (the dead android’s regulator no longer needs sparing her, story 1.9.2). If Markus already has that regulator, only SPARE is offered. Records fromDeadPump and fromDeadPumpSource.

decisions.title: Find Optical Unit, Crane Dumps Bodies, Dig Yourself Out
decisions.context: The AK700 head in the wall: “Hello. I’m an AK700 android…”; a crane dumps bodies on Markus; he digs out and takes its eye, OPTICAL UNIT #8087q - BLUE IRIS: “My program has detected an anomaly. Please contact the nearest CyberLife maintenance center.”

options.label: FIND OPTICAL UNIT
options.effect: Vision and scanning restored; the blue eye stays for the rest of the game.

decisions.note: Chart nodes FIND OPTICAL UNIT, CRANE DUMPS BODIES (event) and DIG YOURSELF OUT, which always follow one another.

benchmark.note: One hub option covering the three nodes.

decisions.title: Find Audio Processor
decisions.context: A head on the right side of the area: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4903 FUNCTIONAL COMPATIBLE; the storm becomes deafening.

decisions.title: Find Pump Regulator in Dead Android
decisions.context: A dead android near the slope: THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR #2886 FUNCTIONAL COMPATIBLE.

options.label: FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN DEAD ANDROID

decisions.gate: PowerPyx: if Markus did not kill the android in the middle for her pump (or never found her); found by scanning.
decisions.note: Chart node FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN DEAD ANDROID.

benchmark.note: Hub option once the new eye can scan, whether or not Markus met her (PowerPyx: “or you never found it in the first place”; story 1.9.1 required SPARE first).

decisions.title: Climb Slope and Markus Came Back from the Dead
decisions.context: Markus climbs the slippery slope, pulls out his LED so he passes for human, and walks toward the city: “My name is Markus.”

options.label: CLIMB SLOPE
options.effect: Ending MARKUS CAME BACK FROM THE DEAD, the only one.

decisions.note: Chart node CLIMB SLOPE and the ending tile MARKUS CAME BACK FROM THE DEAD (no icon). The template marks the line “Markus.” unused.

benchmark.note: The hub’s last option, then a narrated ending event; records fromDeadOutcome and fromDeadLedRemoved.
